question_resolved: Which checks can be done without a laboratory, and which preparation and endpoint are fixed first?
preparation_and_conditions: Existing records only: UniProt sequences for PI4KIIalpha residues 9 and 51 across human, mouse and rat; public Wwox-null or Syn1-Cre deposits for Gsk3a, Gsk3b and Pi4k2a transcript level (transcript is not protein or activity); NMDA package X0 values (perfusate Mg2+, burst rate, burst duration unit)
readouts_and_controls: list of conserved or unconserved residues; expression of the three genes as a transcript-only note; endpoint chosen from the NMDA package
discriminating_result: residue conservation known or listed as unknown; expression noted without inference to activity
in_silico_or_laboratory: in_silico (not run in this package; reopen item)
note: If the residues are not conserved in the species used, the S9/51A construct logic changes.

question_resolved: Is GSK3 activity, by substrate, different in WWOX-deficient neurons, and in which isoform?
preparation_and_conditions: Neurons or cortical slices from the neuron-targeted Wwox deletion (Synapsin I-Cre, S-KO) or null, with littermate or isogenic control; the stage of the burst phenotype (postnatal day 13 to 17 for slices); a WWOX-restored arm where practicable as a biological control
arms: genotype contrast only, no compound; sex recorded; one animal or culture preparation is the unit
readouts_and_controls: Ser9 and Ser21 (both isoforms), Tyr216 and Tyr279, total GSK3 alpha and beta, phospho-glycogen synthase, tau, beta-catenin (phospho Ser33/37/Thr41 and total), phospho-PI4KIIalpha if an antibody exists; several animals per genotype; loading control
discriminating_result: a difference in substrate phosphorylation in the same direction as Ser9 would put the premise on firmer ground; no difference means the knock-out blot (single lane) is not carried and a GSK3 lever would rest on the NMDAR branch alone, independent of WWOX-specific dysregulation
note: Priority question, as in earlier packages: this step changes whether GSK3 is a WWOX-linked lever or only a way to lower NMDAR current.

question_resolved: Does a GSK3-route reduction of bursts do more than a matched plain reduction of NMDAR current, and is the lithium effect GSK3-dependent?
preparation_and_conditions: Acute exposure (minutes to hours) in bursting S-KO slices, with wild-type slices and time-matched vehicle; conditions of the NMDA package X2 (Mg2+ and temperature stated); isolated NMDAR EPSC and AMPA EPSC measured in the same cells
arms: vehicle; lithium (reference); dual inhibitor CT99021; BRD0705 (alpha), BRD3731 (beta) and inactive BRD5648 at the lowest concentration with verified isoform engagement; d-APV titration at the same measured fractional NMDAR reduction (shared with the NMDA package X2)
readouts_and_controls: burst incidence and duration against measured NMDAR current removed; evoked AMPA-only response and stimulus-response relation; wild-type response at the same current reduction; Tyr279 and Tyr216 per isoform and a substrate read in tissue after the run; viability markers; concentration series so that loss of selectivity near the cellular Kd is visible
discriminating_result: IF the GSK3-route compounds lower bursts at a smaller NMDAR reduction than d-APV, or in an isoform-selective pattern, the branch is more than plain suppression. IF the curves coincide with d-APV, the effect is current reduction and GSK3 adds a route to it. IF lithium persists where the inhibitors do not, or persists after GSK3A and GSK3B knock-down (X4), it is not GSK3-dependent
note: Arms are limited to one reference (lithium), one dual tool, one matched isoform pair with its inactive control, and the shared matched-current arm; no further compounds are added.

question_resolved: Is the GSK3-PI4KIIalpha branch the part of the GSK3 effect that touches NMDAR current and bursts?
preparation_and_conditions: Acute, in cultured neurons or organotypic slices where biolistic or viral delivery is possible; paired transfected and neighbouring untransfected cells
arms: shRNA against PI4K2A; shRNA plus shRNA-resistant wild type; shRNA plus S9/51A; each with and without the dual inhibitor; a second NMDAR-lowering manipulation (d-APV at a small matched fraction) added after knock-down to show the system is not at a floor
readouts_and_controls: isolated NMDAR EPSC; AMPA EPSC; burst readout if the preparation bursts (organotypic bursting is not established and is unknown); beta-catenin level in the same culture; viability
discriminating_result: Occlusion of the inhibitor after knock-down, rescue by wild type and not by S9/51A, a preserved response to d-APV (no floor), and unchanged AMPA current would support the branch; a residual inhibitor effect after knock-down, or an inhibitor effect on bursts not occluded, places part of the effect elsewhere
note: Genetic tool only: a drug selective for the branch is not available in the sources read. Occlusion alone does not prove a linear pathway.

question_resolved: Does the compound effect depend on the target it is assigned to?
preparation_and_conditions: Neurons with GSK3A or GSK3B knock-down or knockout (acute where possible), with their controls
arms: the X2 compounds applied to the isoform-depleted cultures, following the isogenic knockout design of the alpha-selective probe paper
readouts_and_controls: the same endpoint and target-engagement readouts as X2; compensation by the other isoform measured
discriminating_result: an effect of an alpha-selective compound that disappears in GSK3A-depleted neurons and an effect of lithium that does not would separate the two; an effect that survives depletion of either isoform points to other targets or to the other isoform
note: A constitutive knockout can induce compensation; acute depletion is preferred and its efficiency must be shown.

question_resolved: What does prolonged exposure do to viability, maturation and beta-catenin, separately from the acute result?
preparation_and_conditions: Prolonged exposure in the same system, over a period chosen from the maturation endpoint, not from the acute window; the oligodendroglial maturation read-out is taken from the myelin package co-culture (X1 and X2 there) and not duplicated here
arms: vehicle; the compound or compounds that passed X2 at the verified engagement level; wild-type control
readouts_and_controls: cell number, viability, neurite or synaptic markers, beta-catenin and an activity reporter where interpretable, maturation markers in the co-culture; a non-significant result is reported as not excluding damage
discriminating_result: absence of change in a limited readout is not safety; a change in beta-catenin is a signalling change whose function must be tested; the decision is only to continue or to stop
note: No post-development window is assumed without risk; a restored-WWOX arm is a biological control and not a solution.
